item.description: Padres' Adrian Morejon gets $88 million comparison to Astros All-Star originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon is now a free agent after a dominant season with the San Diego Padres . If someone's ready to step into a closer's role, it's Morejon. He posted a 2.83 ERA and struck out 30.4% of the batters he faced in 76 appearances (86 innings) in 2026. Morejon's value is higher than most setup men because he can pitch multiple innings. Plus, his Baseball Savant page is a sea of red, including a 99.4 mph average fastball velocity that ranks in the 98th percentile. ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projects the 27-year-old will earn a four-year, $88 million contract in free agency. "He now has a sparkling three-year span of relief performance, hitting the market heading into his age-28 season," McDaniel wrote. McDaniel compared Morejon's performance to Josh Hader's before he signed a five-year, $95 million contract with the Houston Astros . "I'm hedging a bit because Morejon's overall case is a bit stronger, but Hader's real edge (and the recipient of the biggest reliever contract of all time: Edwin Diaz at five years, $102 million) is that saves total," he added. However, Morejon's 6.2 WAR is 1.1 higher than Hader's WAR, mostly due to injuries. Both pitchers are dominant, but Morejon stands out as one of the game's best relievers in the past few seasons. He can continue his role as a dominant setup man or become a full-time closer for the first time. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The North Carolina basketball team struggled in Michael Malone ’s debut as head coach. North Carolina defeated Western Carolina, 80-72, on Monday. Malone made a humorous statement to reporters after the win. “You guys have as much fun as I did?” Malone said, per the Associated Press. “Welcome to the roller coaster.” The Tar Heels pulled away in the last minutes of the second half to win the game. It definitely wasn’t a perfect start, as North Carolina shot just 30 percent from three-point range. The club also struggled with rebounding. But the emotions were I’m thankful to get that first one.” Malone joined the Tar Heels after spending time coaching in the NBA. He is not a typical North Carolina head basketball coach. “Malone is first North Carolina coach to lead the program without having played for the Tar Heels or working as an assistant on staff since Frank McGuire took over in 1952,” the AP reported. Malone’s team has 11 new players. The North Carolina coach says it will take time for his guys to gel. “It’s going to be probably a different guy for us every night,” Malone said. “And we have to stop fighting that sometimes. item.title: Dan Hurley chucks 200th-win ball as UConn men’s basketball eyes bigger goals
item.description: HARTFORD — When the final buzzer sounded and UConn came out victorious in its season opener against Gardner-Webb , Dan Hurley reached a milestone accomplishment. Hurley , who is now in his ninth year with the program, earned win No. 200 as head coach of the UConn Huskies. He sits third on the school’s career wins list behind Jim Calhoun and Hugh Greer. It’s the type of accomplishment that only adds to Hurley’s legacy. One that already includes two national titles and three NCAA championship game appearances. So surely, he took a moment to soak it all in, right? Wrong. “I took the 200-win ball they gave me, and I threw it out the door into the hallway,” Hurley said after Monday’s 86-46 win over Gardner-Webb . “I don't want that (expletive). I don’t care. What am I going to do with that?” The comments illuminate what Hurley’s ultimate goal has always been. It’s not that Hurley isn’t proud of what he’s built in Storrs. It’s that he’s too consumed with what’s next. The only thing that matters is the one thing that is still ahead: a national championship. And the path that Hurley took to get here has made him even hungrier to add to a résumé that would already put him in the hall of fame. “I wasn't some preordained golden boy coach that started getting these big jobs at a young age. I grinded it out at the college level,” Hurley said. "I grinded it out at Wagner. I had to go to a mid-major. I've only really been coaching at this big level for nine years.” Looking at Monday’s box score, one would think the Huskies played a dominant game from start to finish. The Huskies beat Gardner-Webb by 40 points. They outrebounded the Runnin’ Bulldogs 46-28, held them to 26% shooting from the field and turned 17 turnovers into 14 points. But the message from Hurley after the game wasn’t about how well he thought his team played. It was about all the things he thought they didn’t do. “It’s probably a frustrating game,” Hurley said. “I think we're a better 3-point shooting team than 9-for-29. I think we're a better free-throw shooting team than 15-for-24. I hated the way we ended the first half. I thought that was really low level. And then to get only nine offensive rebounds in the game, it's really disappointing.” While the comments might seem over the top, Hurley’s words were necessary. item.title: Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision
item.description: Spanish striker Jesus de Miguel died Tuesday at a hospital in Santa Cruz de Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain. File Photo by Ramon de la Rocha/EPA Nov. 3 (UPI) -- CD Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after a collision during a Spanish second-division soccer match, the club announced Tuesday. De Miguel, 30, collided with FC Andorra goalie Jesus Owono in stoppage time of a match with Andorra on Monday in Tenerife. The match, which was tied 2-2, was abandoned. De Miguel was taken to the ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria after the incident. Tenerife first said he was in "stable" condition, but later announced that his condition "worsened neurologically. He died at 8 a.m. local time at the Santa Cruz facility on the largest of the Canary Islands. "There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness," Tenerife said. "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones, alongside all of Tinerfenismo that today weeps for this cruel outcome. "The family of Jesus de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments." De Miguel was chasing down a long pass near midfield during the sequence. Owono collided with with the striker as he attempted to defend the play. Medical personnel tended to the Spanish striker, who was motionless on the ground, before was taken to the hospital. Andorra and several other clubs offered condolences to de Miguel and his family in the wake of the tragedy. "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife," Andorra said. "Rest in peace." The Royal Spanish Football Federation also said matches are suspended Tuesday due to de Miguel's death. All UEFA matches this week, including those in the Champions League and Europa League, will include a moment of silence for the Spanish striker. "Spanish football mourns the loss of Jesus de Miguel," the RFEF said. "Devastated by the sad news, from the RFEF we wish to express our deepest sorrow for his passing today.We extend our most heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to Tenerife and all its fans, whom we accompany in these moments of profound grief. "Rest in peace."

item.title: Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles
item.description: Cam Skattebo | Getty Images Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team’s Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo’s injury in more detail. “It’s going to be probably day to day up to the game,” Harbaugh said. ”We’re going to just have to see where we’re at. I’ll probably have more information toward the end of the week. We’ll see on both those guys where we’re at.“ Skattebo has had an up-and-down season for the Giants. He scored a touchdown in the team’s Week 1 win against the Dallas Cowboys, but struggled to find the end zone in the next four weeks. He also recorded four fumbles in the team’s first five games. His struggles led to him being benched in the team’s Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Skattebo likely will have a big role when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles this week if he is able to go. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation.

item.title: Organizing Committee confirm 2027 Asian Cup decision amid Middle East conflict
item.description: The 2027 Asian Cup has officially been postponed -Credit:GIUSEPPE CACACE, AFP via Getty Images The 2027 AFC Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia has been pushed back by 11 months, with the final now scheduled to take place in 2028, owing to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. An announcement, which had been anticipated for weeks, has been confirmed by organizers, who have set a new start date of December 23 next year. The tournament will wrap up on January 21. The proposed new dates still require FIFA approval, but hosting the event in Saudi Arabia had become increasingly untenable following the Riyadh airport attack carried out by Iran-backed Houthi rebels from Yemen. A statement read, via The Mirror : "The Organising Committee for AFC Asian Cup approved to reschedule the flagship national team tournament in light of the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions. The new dates of the tournament will be presented to FIFA for approval. "Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the Competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders. item.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Running Back Targets: Tyler Allgeier, Mike Washington Jr, And More Options
item.description: Arizona Cardinals receiver Tyler Allgeier (22) is introduced before their game against the Denver Broncos at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect With Week 8 now behind us, it's time to turn our attention to Week 9. As always, that starts with the waiver wire. This is a big week for running backs, and there are quite a few potential studs to choose from. We will help you decide which ones to prioritize. These are the top running back waiver wire targets for Week 9. Running Back Waiver Wire Targets: Week 9 RB Tyler Allgeier, Arizona Cardinals With Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight both going down with injuries early in Week 8, Allgeier exploded. He rushed for 147 yards and a touchdown, and caught five passes for 44 yards and another touchdown. Love and Knight could both miss time, and we wouldn't expect either to play this week. Knight went down with a brutal concussion, and Love injured his right ankle right after returning from a left ankle injury. If you need a starter this week or over the next few weeks, Allgeier is the running back to target on the waiver wire. However, his upside does have an ex,piration date. Even if Love goes on injured reserve, once he comes back, he's the lead back. Knight's return will damage, but not destroy Allgeier's value. RB Mike Washington Jr, Las Vegas Raiders Washington seems to have overtaken the backfield in Las Vegas, with Ashton Jeanty being relegated to a change-of-pace and pass-catching role. Jeanty carried the ball just two times, while Washington handled 25 carries. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak insists that Jeanty isn't hurt; despite him being a known liar, we kind of have to take him at his word. Which means either Washington has earned the starting job or Jeanty is hurt and they aren't giving him a chance to get healthy. In either case, Washington could maintain the lead-back role in Las Vegas for the remainder of the season and is the best long-term add on the waiver wire this week. RB Emmett Johnson, Kansas City Chiefs Johnson had a breakout game in Week 8, which was overshadowed by Jonah Coleman breaking out in the same game. item.title: ‘Weakest Call’: Patrick Mahomes’ Wife Brittany Blasts Referees After Chiefs’ Loss to Broncos
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes has recorded 1,795 passing yards, 12 passing touchdowns, and eight interceptions across the 2026 season. He has also added 77 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown on 21 carries. The aftermath of Kansas City’s 28–24 loss to the Denver Broncos shifted attention to a late false-start call. Brittany Mahomes, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, criticized the decision on social media after the penalty erased a potential game-winning touchdown. Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City face scrutiny after controversial late-game penalties The penalty erased a touchdown that would have put Kansas City ahead at the final whistle. Moore’s movement became the central question after the game. Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) reacts before the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images The call came with four seconds left after Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice in the end zone. Brittany Mahomes wrote , “You can’t tell me you call that on a game winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it’s us. That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can’t tell me otherwise.” The flag went against right tackle Jaylon Moore before the snap. It moved Kansas City back five yards and added four seconds to the clock. Mahomes was sacked on the next play, ending the Chiefs’ final possession. Andy Reid said he did not see a false start on the play. “I didn’t see it,” Reid said . “That’s one man’s opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn’t see a false start.” Moore also appeared to move a leg before the snap, according to the postgame report. Mahomes completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. The fourth-quarter collapse and penalty total defined the loss. Kansas City committed 11 penalties for 105 yards. Denver finished with six penalties for 45 yards. The Chiefs also missed a 54-yard field-goal attempt by Harrison Butker before Denver scored the go-ahead touchdown. Denver erased an 11-point deficit with two fourth-quarter drives . Bo Nix hit Nate Adkins, then found Jaylen Waddle for the two-point conversion. Jonah Coleman’s 51-yard run set up the winning score. Kansas City hosts the New York Jets next Sunday. The Chiefs will need cleaner execution and fewer penalties moving forward as they prepare to host the Jets. item.description: A remarkable head-to-head trend continued Sunday, as the Arizona Cardinals defeated the Dallas Cowboys 33-30 in overtime and added another chapter to a long-running matchup. Since 2008, Dallas has won only once in 10 meetings with Arizona, a record that makes the opponent a persistent problem for the franchise. The latest result appeared unlikely for much of the afternoon, with Dallas holding a two-score lead and its defense producing two takeaways and five sacks. The home team went into the second half ahead 14-3, then extended the margin to 24-10 early in the fourth quarter after quarterback Dak Prescott scrambled for a touchdown. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-USA TODAY Sports The momentum changed when Gardner Minshew replaced Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter. Minshew quickly energized the offense, throwing three touchdown passes without an interception and completing 17 of 23 attempts for 188 yards. Running back Tyler Allgeier also took advantage of the opportunity, finishing with 147 rushing yards on 11 carries and adding a touchdown reception. The switch followed a difficult first half, when the offense struggled to sustain drives and managed only a field goal before halftime. Arizona steadily erased the deficit, with Allgeier scoring on a 63-yard run and later catching a five-yard touchdown pass. Minshew also connected with tight end Trey McBride for a 14-yard score, bringing the visitors within three points. Dallas answered with a field goal, but left the door open for a final possession. Chad Ryland missed the extra point that could have won it in regulation, sending the contest to overtime, where both teams punted on their first possessions before Ryland redeemed himself with a 42-yard field goal. The comeback gave Arizona a 3-5 record and dropped Dallas to 3-5, while the historic matchup statistic remained a striking reminder of the teams’ uneven series. A game that seemed firmly in Dallas’ control became another painful loss, with the late collapse underscoring how difficult the Cardinals have been to put away. item.title: How Do Football Recruiting Rankings Work? Stars and Ratings Explained
item.description: Football recruiting rankings work by comparing high school players based on their projected college potential. Scouts study game film, physical measurements, athletic testing, production and other information, then assign grades and rank prospects among their respective position groups, both nationally and within their state. At Rivals, we view the NFL Draft as the most accurate gauge of a college football player’s performance and ability. Thus, NFL Draft potential is a major driver of the Rivals football prospect rankings, particularly from a national perspective. The rankings process is highly intensive and involves much more than simply counting touchdowns and scholarship offers or a fast 40-yard dash. Evaluators consider how all of the available evidence fits together and how a player’s abilities could translate against better competition. For athletes and parents, understanding that process can help put stars in perspective, explain ranking changes and guide decisions about development, camps and college opportunities. What is the difference between a rating, stars and a ranking? These terms are related, but each answers a different question. Term What it means Example Rating A numerical scouting grade reflecting evaluated potential. A Rivals grade of 91. Star rating A category associated with a range of grades. A four-star prospect. Ranking A player’s placement relative to other prospects in a defined group. No. 150 nationally or No. 20 at his position. A player can hold national, position and state rankings simultaneously. Those numbers describe different comparisons of the same athlete. A grade and a ranking can also move differently. A player could improve his grade while falling in the rankings if other prospects improve more. Who determines football recruiting rankings? Recruiting services employ scouts and analysts to evaluate players and build their rankings. Each organization makes its own assessments, so the same prospect can have different grades or placements across services. Rivals’ process involves several stages: Identifying prospects – Rivals evaluates more than 10,000 prospects annually across three recruiting cycles for potential three-, four- and five-star recognition. Collecting evidence – Scouts combine their evaluations with measurements, athletic data, historical trends and feedback gathered through relationships with college coaches and recruiting personnel. Assigning ratings – A ratings committee made up of the national recruiting team assigns player grades. Auditing the release – A separate review checks that the established process and protocols were followed before publication. item.title: NASCAR just landed new manufacturer for 2027 Daytona 500 and beyond
item.description: Historically short runway? Who cares, land the plane. That’s the philosophy for Dodge, which will return to NASCAR’s Cup Series next season, ending a 14-year absence from America’s top stock-car circuit. Yes, these things are normally announced more than a year ahead of a return, given all it takes to put together a full-time racing effort. But Dodge and parent company Stellantis are going from official announcement to the Daytona starting grid in just three months. “Sure, we could spend three years planning, testing and perfecting … or we could do all three in real time, on the track,” Tim Kuniskis, head of Dodge’s North America racing interests, announced this week at the big Las Vegas auto industry showcase — SEMA. “It’s going to be exponentially harder this way. But slow has never been part of Dodge DNA.” Who will drive and who will supply the horses for Dodge? Dodge returned to NASCAR’s Truck Series this year with a five-truck effort out of Kaulig Racing’s shop, and Kaulig will remain the partner for 2027 and beyond with its two-car Cup Series organization. The current Cup Series drivers for Kaulig are AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon. The team will officially announce its two-driver lineup Saturday for the switch from Chevrolet to Dodge. Dodge will be able to build a pair of Chargers in time for the Feb. 21 Daytona 500, but will have to purchase and/or lease engines from a different manufacturer until Stellantis gets its engine effort in gear. It’s believed the team will buy Chevy engines from Richard Childress Racing’s engine division while Dodge goes through the process of developing its own engines that meet NASCAR Cup Series specs. You thought this story was over. It's only just begun. @Dodge returns to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027! pic.twitter.com/hrmq1WwqVB — NASCAR (@NASCAR) November 3, 2026 Given the hurried and start-up nature, don’t expect Dodge to pick up where it left off in 2012, when Brad Keselowski drove a Dodge to the Cup Series championship. That season ended a 12-year run for Dodge, which had returned to the big-league circuit with a big splash in 2001. This move once again gives the Cup Series four full-time manufacturers, with Dodge joining Chevy, Ford and Toyota. It’s the consequence of talent, hard work, passion, and the daily efforts of a lot of people down the years. Seeing Niko experience that moment fills us with great joy and pride.” Eintracht head coach Adi Hütter said: “The door is open here at Eintracht – [we’ve had] Elias Baum, Jeremiaha Maluze, and now Niko Ilicevic. Mandatory Credit: Vasha Hunt-Imagn Images The 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Championship 4 is not a real thing this year because the format changed. Only three drivers remain in the hunt for the title after the final race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Per Beyond the Flag, Kyle Larson holds a massive 67-point lead over Christopher Bell and a 70-point lead over Denny Hamlin. Larson needs almost nothing to go wrong to win back-to-back titles. The old four-driver final round is dead for 2026. If the pre-2026 format still existed, the field would look very different right now. Tyler Reddick would have locked his spot with a win at Phoenix Raceway three races ago. Larson would have punched his ticket too with a win at Talladega Superspeedway, according to Beyond the Flag . Sunday’s victory at Martinsville Speedway would have been replicated by William Byron. That means Reddick, Larson, and Byron would be in the final four for sure. Hamlin would have squeezed in as the fourth driver on points. A Format Change That Broke The Drama The new rules strip away the guaranteed four-driver showdown fans love to watch. Under the old system, the Championship 4 was set after three rounds of three races. Now, the math allows for a three-man fight if one driver leads by enough points. Larson owns a 67-point gap over Bell. He owns a 70-point gap over Hamlin. The race has 76 points up for grabs in the 267-lap event. That margin is too big for the other two to overcome without a miracle. It hurts the storylines to see a one-sided battle in the finale. item.description: Sam Smith joined Wrexham from Reading in January 2025 [Getty Images] Wrexham forward Sam Smith is facing a "significant" spell out of action due to a knee injury, manager Phil Parkinson has confirmed. Smith suffered the injury during Wrexham's 1-0 defeat at Sheffield United in the Championship on Friday. The 28-year-old will see a specialist later on Tuesday to discover the extent of the damage and the duration of his absence. "Unfortunately for... it looks like he's going to face a significant period on the sidelines," Parkinson said. "He came off against Sheffield and went back and carried on and his knee swelled up significantly the next day. "He sees a specialist this afternoon (Tuesday) and we will know more then. "Our initial thoughts are that he could need surgery, but we'll know more after today." Smith's injury is a further blow to Parkinson and his team before they host Championship leaders Middlesbrough on Wednesday (19:45 GMT). Forwards Josh Windass and Nathan Broadhead are still sidelined while Callum O'Hare remains a doubt after missing the loss at Bramall Lane. Parkinson said their absence presents an opportunity for others including youngster Bailey Cadamarteri, the Jamaica international. The 21-year-old, who joined from Sheffield Wednesday in January, has yet to start a senior game for the Dragons with his five appearances this season coming off the bench. "That's what happens in football clubs, people come out of the side and other people say, 'this is my chance to step up to the plate and show what I'm all about'," Parkinson added. "Undoubtedly Bailey's going to get some game time and I'm looking forward to seeing that. "Bailey's ready and chomping at the bit and with Sam's injury he's going to get an opportunity and more game time. "He's trained well and he's ready."
